symbols.doc: Define the editor command :NAME as the procedure PROC applied to the words typed after it. Only while init.scm loads.
symbols.name: define-command

symbols.doc: Define the theme NAME, usable with :theme and set-theme. SPEC is a list of ("key" . value) pairs: base names the built-in theme to start from (mocha when left out), every other key sets one palette entry to a "#rrggbb" colour or "default", and bold-keywords takes #t or #f. Only while init.scm loads.
symbols.name: define-theme

symbols.doc: Start the editor with the theme NAME, a built-in one or one define-theme made. Only while init.scm loads.
symbols.name: set-theme

symbols.doc: True if the command was started from a Visual selection and no edit has happened yet.
symbols.name: selection?

symbols.doc: The selected text: v selections include each newline they cross, V selections are whole lines joined with newlines.
symbols.name: selection-text

symbols.doc: The text of lines START to END of the buffer, 1-based and inclusive, END defaulting to START, joined with newlines.
symbols.name: buffer-text

symbols.doc: The number of lines in the buffer.
symbols.name: line-count

symbols.doc: The 1-based line of the cursor, which is the end of the selection when there is one.
symbols.name: cursor-line

symbols.doc: Replace the selection with TEXT. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT.
symbols.name: replace-selection

symbols.doc: Insert TEXT before the cursor character. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT.
symbols.name: insert-text

symbols.doc: Set the status line shown when the command finishes; the last call wins.
symbols.name: message

symbols.doc: Run the procedure HANDLER with each value that arrives on CHANNEL, as a command of its own with a fresh copy of the buffer, until the channel is closed. CHANNEL should be buffered (make-channel n), because a send on an unbuffered one waits for a receiver and the editor never waits. A handler runs when the editor is in Normal mode with nothing pending; until then values stay in the channel. :reload drops it.
symbols.name: on-channel

symbols.doc: Run the procedure HANDLER with TASK when it finishes, as a command of its own with a fresh copy of the buffer. TASK is one made by spawn-detached, which keeps running after this command ends. Inside HANDLER, (task-wait task) gives the task's value or raises its error, so guard works as usual. A task that is cancelled (task-cancel!, :reload, quitting) does not run its handler. A handler runs when the editor is in Normal mode with nothing pending; until then it waits. :reload drops it and ends the task.
symbols.name: on-done

symbols.doc: A channel that receives #t once, SECONDS from now (0.01 to 604800), kept by the editor. Brote's own (after secs) ends with the command that made it, so use this one to wait across commands: (on-channel (timer 60) handler). :reload drops it.
symbols.name: timer

symbols.doc: Show a window listing ITEMS to choose from, and return a channel. Typing narrows the list, Enter chooses, Esc cancels. An item is a string, or a pair (label . value) to show the label and send the value. The channel receives the choice and is then closed; a cancelled window closes it with nothing sent. Use it with on-channel.
symbols.name: show-list

symbols.doc: Show a read-only window with LINES, a string or a list of strings, and return a channel that is closed when it is dismissed with Enter, q or Esc. Long lines wrap.
symbols.name: show-text

symbols.doc: Ask for a line of text and return a channel. Enter sends the text, Ctrl-U clears it, Esc cancels. The channel is closed after the answer; a cancelled prompt closes it with nothing sent.
symbols.name: prompt

symbols.doc: Bind a key in MODE to the procedure PROC, which runs as a command does, with no arguments. KEY is one character such as "x", Ctrl and a lowercase letter such as "<C-x>", or Alt and a character such as "<A-x>". A key the editor already uses needs OVERRIDE to be #t. Only while init.scm loads.
symbols.name: bind-key

symbols.doc: Run the procedure PROC once, with no arguments and as a command does, after the editor has started and a file is open. Only while init.scm loads, and once.
symbols.name: on-start

symbols.doc: The path of the file being edited, or "" when the buffer has no file.
symbols.name: buffer-path

symbols.doc: The 1-based column of the cursor, counted in characters.
symbols.name: cursor-column

symbols.doc: The mode the command was started from: "normal", "visual" or "visual-line".
symbols.name: mode

symbols.doc: The selection as the list (START-LINE START-COLUMN END-LINE END-COLUMN), 1-based and inclusive at both ends, or #f when there is no selection or an edit has ended it. A V selection runs from the first column of its first line to the last character of its last.
symbols.name: selection-range

symbols.doc: The word under the cursor: the letters, digits and underscores around it on its line. It is "" when the cursor is on anything else.
symbols.name: word-at-cursor

symbols.doc: Where the word under the cursor is, as the list (LINE START-COLUMN END-COLUMN), 1-based and inclusive at both ends like selection-range, or #f when the cursor is not on a letter, digit or underscore. (string-length (word-at-cursor)) is END-COLUMN - START-COLUMN + 1.
symbols.name: word-range

symbols.doc: The first place TEXT occurs at or after the position (LINE COLUMN), as the list (LINE COLUMN), or #f. The search is literal, case-sensitive and does not wrap; LINE and COLUMN default to the start of the buffer, and TEXT must be on one line.
symbols.name: find

symbols.doc: A mark at LINE and COLUMN, 1-based, that stays with the text around it as the buffer changes, so a handler that runs later can still find the place. At most 256 are alive at once; marks nothing refers to any more are freed. Text typed exactly at a mark goes after it.
symbols.name: mark-at

symbols.doc: The 1-based line a mark is on now.
symbols.name: mark-line

symbols.doc: The 1-based column a mark is on now.
symbols.name: mark-column

symbols.doc: True if the text the mark was on has been replaced since it was made, so it only stands for the nearest place. A mark that only moved with its text is not disturbed.
symbols.name: mark-disturbed?

symbols.doc: Insert TEXT at a mark, as insert-at does at a line and column. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT. Ends the selection.
symbols.name: insert-at-mark

symbols.doc: Replace the text EXPECTED, which must be exactly what is at a mark now, with TEXT. If the text there is something else, for example because the word was edited since the mark was made, it is an error that says what is there and nothing changes. TEXT may be empty, which deletes EXPECTED. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT. Ends the selection.
symbols.name: replace-at-mark

symbols.doc: Move the cursor to a mark, as set-cursor does. It does not end the selection.
symbols.name: goto-mark

symbols.doc: Replace lines START to END, 1-based and inclusive, with TEXT, which may hold any number of lines; "" leaves one empty line. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT. Ends the selection.
symbols.name: replace-lines

symbols.doc: Delete lines START to END, 1-based and inclusive. Deleting every line leaves one empty line. The cursor ends on the first column of the line that took the place of the first deleted one, or of the last line. Ends the selection.
symbols.name: delete-lines

symbols.doc: Insert TEXT before the character at LINE and COLUMN, 1-based; the column one past the end of a line appends to it. TEXT may hold several lines. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT. Ends the selection.
symbols.name: insert-at

symbols.doc: Move the cursor to LINE and COLUMN, 1-based; a column one past the end of a line puts it on the last character, as in Normal mode. It does not end the selection: the selection then runs from where it started to the new cursor.
symbols.name: set-cursor

symbols.doc: The string that Base64 text stands for. An error if the text is not Base64, or decodes to bytes that are not UTF-8 text (strings are text).
symbols.name: base64-decode

symbols.doc: The Base64 text of a string's UTF-8 bytes. With #t as the second argument, the URL-safe alphabet without padding.
symbols.name: base64-encode

symbols.doc: CSV text for a list of rows, each a list of strings or numbers (quoted where needed, one line per row).
symbols.name: csv-emit

symbols.doc: Parse CSV text (RFC 4180) into a list of rows, each a list of strings. The optional delimiter is a one-character string, "," by default.
symbols.name: csv-parse

symbols.doc: The ECDSA P-256 signature of a message's SHA-256 under a private key, as DER hex: the deterministic signature of RFC 6979, the same for the same key and message. The key is a 32-byte scalar, as hex.
symbols.name: ecdsa-sign

symbols.doc: Whether a message's ECDSA P-256 signature (DER hex) verifies under a public key (a compressed point, hex). The key must be one the policy granted with (digest (keys …)); a signature that does not verify is #f, a key the policy does not grant is an error.
symbols.name: ecdsa-verify

symbols.doc: The Ed25519 signature of a message under a private key, as lower-case hex. The key is 64 bytes (a full private key) or 32 bytes (a seed), as hex.
symbols.name: ed25519-sign

symbols.doc: Whether a message's Ed25519 signature verifies under a public key (32 bytes, hex). The key must be one the policy granted with (digest (keys …)); a signature that does not verify is #f, a key the policy does not grant is an error.
symbols.name: ed25519-verify

symbols.doc: Add a string to the end of a file, creating it if needed.
symbols.name: fs-append-text

symbols.doc: True when the path names a file or directory, #f when it does not. A path outside the granted directories is an error, not #f.
symbols.name: fs-exists?

symbols.doc: The names in a directory, sorted, as a list of strings (not the directory's own path, and not . or ..). Use fs-stat to tell files from directories.
symbols.name: fs-list

symbols.doc: Make a directory and any missing parents inside the granted tree. A directory that exists is fine.
symbols.name: fs-mkdir

symbols.doc: The contents of a file as a string. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD. A file larger than the host's limit is an error.
symbols.name: fs-read-text

symbols.doc: Delete a file or an empty directory. A missing path is an error. There is no recursive delete.
symbols.name: fs-remove

symbols.doc: Move a file or directory to a new path inside the same granted tree, replacing a file already there.
symbols.name: fs-rename

symbols.doc: What a file or directory is, as an association list: "size" (bytes), "dir" (#t for a directory), "mode" (permission bits as text such as "0644") and "mtime" (seconds since 1970, a float). A missing file is an error; see fs-exists?.
symbols.name: fs-stat

symbols.doc: Watch a granted directory for changes, polled every interval seconds (default 1): returns a watch. fs-watch-changes drains the names that appeared, changed (size or modification time) or were removed, and fs-watch-stop! ends the watch. The watch runs until stopped or the host closes the runtime, not only until the evaluation that started it ends.
symbols.name: fs-watch

symbols.doc: The names in a watched directory that appeared, changed or were removed since the last call, sorted, as a list of strings; drains the queue.
symbols.name: fs-watch-changes

symbols.doc: Stop a watch: its goroutine ends. Stopping a stopped watch does nothing.
symbols.name: fs-watch-stop!

symbols.doc: Write a string to a file, creating it or replacing what it held. The directory must exist and be granted for writing.
symbols.name: fs-write-text

symbols.doc: The string that hexadecimal text stands for. An error if it is not hexadecimal or its bytes are not UTF-8 text.
symbols.name: hex-decode

symbols.doc: The lower-case hexadecimal text of a string's UTF-8 bytes.
symbols.name: hex-encode

symbols.doc: The HMAC-SHA-256 of a message under a key, as lower-case hex.
symbols.name: hmac-sha256

symbols.doc: Send an HTTP request and return the response as an association list with "status" (integer), "headers" (an alist with lower-case names), "body" (a string) and "url" (the final URL after redirects). Headers are an alist such as '(("accept" . "text/plain")). A status of 400 or more is a result, not an error; a refused host, method, redirect, a body past the host's limit or a timeout is an error.
symbols.name: http-request

symbols.doc: Parse INI text into a list of (section entries...) pairs in order of first appearance: [section] headers, key=value lines, ; or # comment lines, and a valueless key whose value is "". Keys before any header are in the "" section. Whitespace around names and values is stripped and a duplicate key keeps its last value.
symbols.name: ini-parse

symbols.doc: The MD5 digest of a string's UTF-8 bytes, as lower-case hex. Broken for security; for checksums and compatibility.
symbols.name: md5

symbols.doc: Run a program and wait for it. The argument is a list of strings, the command first; it is started directly, never through a shell, so no argument is interpreted. Returns an association list with "exit-code" (integer; -1 if a signal ended it), "stdout" and "stderr" (strings). A nonzero exit is a result, not an error; a command the host did not grant, one that cannot start, a timeout, or output past the host's limit is an error. Options is an alist: "stdin" (a string to feed it) and "timeout" (seconds, at most the host's limit). The program sees only the environment variables the host granted.
symbols.name: proc-run

symbols.doc: Start an HTTP server on addr ("host:port"; port 0 picks a free one), serving routes, an alist of path to handler procedure. The handler is called with an alist ((method . "GET") (path . "/") (body . "…")) and returns a string (sent with status 200) or a list (status body). Returns a server; see server-address and server-stop!. Loopback addresses are allowed whenever net is granted; any other host must be in the net allow list. Each handler call runs under the context of the evaluation that called serve, so a gate and a per-caller policy see that caller.
symbols.name: serve

symbols.doc: The address a server is bound to, as "host:port" (with the free port serve picked when it was given 0).
symbols.name: server-address

symbols.doc: Stop a server: it closes its listener and answers no more requests. Stopping a stopped server does nothing.
symbols.name: server-stop!

symbols.doc: True for servers.
symbols.name: server?

symbols.doc: The SHA-1 digest of a string's UTF-8 bytes, as lower-case hex. Broken for security; for checksums and compatibility.
symbols.name: sha1

symbols.doc: The SHA-256 digest of a string's UTF-8 bytes, as lower-case hex.
symbols.name: sha256

symbols.doc: The SHA-512 digest of a string's UTF-8 bytes, as lower-case hex.
symbols.name: sha512

symbols.doc: Undo url-encode. An error for a bad % escape.
symbols.name: url-decode

symbols.doc: Escape text for a URL query value (space becomes +, reserved characters %XX).
symbols.name: url-encode

symbols.doc: True for watches.
symbols.name: watch?

symbols.doc: (http-request "GET" url headers): the response as an association list. Needs (requires (net ...)) in the module's header, and runs in a (spawn-detached ...) task, not in a command.
symbols.name: http-get

symbols.doc: (http-request "POST" url headers body): the response as an association list. Needs (requires (net ...)) in the module's header, and runs in a (spawn-detached ...) task, not in a command.
symbols.name: http-post

symbols.doc: The response body of a GET, parsed as JSON. A status of 400 or more is an error. Needs (requires (net ...)) in the module's header, and runs in a (spawn-detached ...) task, not in a command.
symbols.name: http-get-json

symbols.doc: Send value as JSON in a POST and return the parsed JSON reply. A status of 400 or more is an error. Needs (requires (net ...)) in the module's header, and runs in a (spawn-detached ...) task, not in a command.
symbols.name: http-post-json

symbols.doc: Import a module from modules/ beside init.scm; supports only, except, rename and prefix.
symbols.name: require

symbols.doc: Declare the module name, documentation and exported names as the first form of a module.
symbols.name: define-module
